did_you_know.text: Did you know? Hosea describes an attempt to heal Israel, but at that very moment Ephraim’s guilt and Samaria’s crimes are exposed: acts of deceit, theft, and wrongdoing.
Did you know? Hosea compares the people and their leaders to a blazing oven, describing how their passions, adultery, and intrigues grow increasingly intense.

Did you know? According to the chapter, the Israelites’ corruption is directed even against their leaders: they are portrayed as devouring their judges, and all their kings fall; yet no one calls on the LORD.
Did you know? Ephraim is compared to a cake that has not been turned, leaving one side burned. The image conveys a state of imbalance and harm that goes uncorrected.
Did you know? The chapter describes Ephraim as one whose strength is consumed by foreigners, while gray hairs appear on him; yet he is unaware of his weakening.
Did you know? Ephraim is compared to a senseless dove because he turns first to Egypt and then to Assyria instead of turning to the LORD.
Did you know? Because Ephraim has turned to other nations, the LORD describes himself as spreading a net over him and bringing him down, using the image of catching a bird in flight.

Did you know? The people do not truly cry out to the LORD; instead, they wail on their beds and gather around grain and new wine. Thus, the chapter distinguishes between complaining about hardship and genuinely turning to God.
Did you know? Israel’s response is compared to a deceitful bow—a bow that does not work properly or is not aimed correctly—so their officials fall by the sword and their words become a mockery.
